label: Planning, Scheduling & Optimization
definition: Forecast demand, and plan, schedule and optimize how crude oil, feedstocks and refined products move through refineries, terminals and the distribution network, so that supply meets forecast demand at the best margin the operating, inventory and contract limits allow.
scope_note: Includes demand forecasting, refinery production planning, regional and distribution optimization, distribution planning and scheduling with inventory planning, and comparing results with the approved plan and its assumptions. It decides volumes and timing. Buying, selling and trading the barrels belongs to Supply & Trading, and moving and storing them belongs to Midstream & Logistics.
evidence: mpc-10k, Item 1, Refining & Marketing, Refineries: transport links between refineries let intermediates move between them to optimize operations and use processing capacity; mpc-10k, Item 1, Information about our Executive Officers: a Senior Vice President Value Chain Optimization; pbf-10k, Item 1, Information About Our Executive Officers: a Senior Vice President, Supply, Trading and Optimization; psx-10k, Item 7 MD&A, Business Environment: Refining results depend on throughput, feedstock costs and product yields, which the plan sets

label: Supply & Trading
definition: Buy, sell, exchange and trade crude oil, feedstocks and refined products, and manage the resulting commercial positions and their risk through confirmation, actualization and settlement, so that the business has the supply it needs and sells what it makes.
scope_note: Includes crude and feedstock supply, refined product supply, trading, confirmations and risk management, actualization of physical deliveries, settlement and accounting of trades, and the commercial management of product distribution. It decides what is bought, sold and delivered where. Planning volumes and timing belongs to Planning, Scheduling & Optimization, and moving and storing product belongs to Midstream & Logistics. Buying the materials and services the business uses belongs to Procurement & Supply Chain (Goods and Services).
evidence: mpc-10k, Item 1, Refining & Marketing, Crude Oil Supply: crude is obtained through term contracts and spot purchases or exchanges; vlo-10k, Items 1 and 2, Refining, Feedstock Supply: crude and other feedstocks are bought on term and spot contracts; dino-10k, Items 1 and 2, Refinery Operations, Crude Oil and Feedstock Supplies: crude is bought from independent producers and major oil companies; shel-20f, Strategic Report, segment overview: the segment includes trading and optimisation of crude oil, oil products and petrochemicals; paa-10k, Items 1 and 2, Crude Oil Segment: merchant activities buy crude supply and move it to sales locations

label: Midstream & Logistics
definition: Transport, terminal, store and handle crude oil, intermediates and refined products between supply points, refineries, terminals and distribution locations, so that product is where it is needed, in the quantity and quality agreed.
scope_note: Includes pipeline, marine, rail and truck transportation; terminal and tank-farm operations, with the controls on who may lift product at a terminal; storage; blending and additive services outside refinery process units; product segregation; and custody transfer. The asset owner, the asset operator, the service provider and the service customer are separate roles, and one party may hold several. What is bought, sold and delivered belongs to Supply & Trading, and planning volumes and timing belongs to Planning, Scheduling & Optimization. Crude gathering and NGL fractionation are placed here by the scope review (DSBP-DEC-0046) and added by a later batch once their evidence row is cited.
evidence: pbf-10k, Item 1, Logistics: receiving, handling, storage and transferring of crude oil, refined products and intermediates; psx-10k, Item 1, Midstream: transports crude and feedstocks, delivers refined products and provides terminaling and storage; mplx-10k, Item 1, Transportation, Terminal and Storage Services: receipt, storage, throughput, blending and delivery of commodities; paa-10k, Items 1 and 2, Crude Oil Segment: gathering and transporting crude by pipeline, truck, barge or railcar, with terminalling and storage; kmi-10k, Items 1 and 2, Business and Properties: refined products terminals store fuels and offer blending services

label: Procurement & Supply Chain (Goods and Services)
definition: Source, buy and manage the supply of the materials, equipment and services the business uses, such as chemicals, catalysts, maintenance materials and contracted services, and manage the suppliers that provide them, so that operations have what they need at an acceptable cost and risk.
scope_note: Includes supplier selection and contracting, purchasing, category management, supplier performance and risk, and materials management. It does not buy or sell crude oil, feedstocks or refined products, which belongs to Supply & Trading (DSBP-DEC-0012).
evidence: vlo-suppliers: suppliers of goods and services, from chemicals and catalysts to equipment, maintenance materials and services, with strategic sourcing; mpc-sustainability, Supplier Selection Process: procurement teams and category teams manage suppliers of critical goods and services; psx-suppliers, home page: suppliers are brought in through procurement processes

label: Legal & External Affairs
definition: Advise the business on the law and manage its legal risk, govern its corporate affairs, and manage its relations with governments, regulators and the public and its communications with its own people, so that the business acts lawfully and speaks consistently.
scope_note: Includes legal advice; contract, transaction and dispute support; litigation; regulatory and compliance advice; corporate governance, the corporate secretary and entity management; government and regulatory affairs; public, media and community relations; and internal communications. It advises Environment, Health & Safety on legal privilege, enforcement exposure and disclosure when an incident raises them.
evidence: psx-10k, Item 1, Information About Our Executive Officers: one officer holds government affairs, general counsel and corporate secretary; vlo-10k, Items 1 and 2, Information About Our Executive Officers: an Executive Vice President and General Counsel; pbf-10k, Item 1, Information About Our Executive Officers: a Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary; mpc-10k, Item 1, Information about our Executive Officers: a Chief Legal Officer, and communications held with human resources

label: Environment, Health & Safety
scope_note: This domain governs EHS management, environmental and safety compliance, required regulator-facing reporting, and the enterprise coordination of incidents, releases, investigations, corrective actions, and emergency response. It does not replace operational ownership: operating sites, asset owners, maintenance, logistics, product stewardship, and business functions remain accountable for safely executing their work, preventing and containing events, and completing assigned corrective actions. Legal & External Affairs advises on legal privilege, enforcement exposure, disclosure, litigation hold, regulator strategy, and approved internal and external communications when those dimensions arise. Enterprise Risk Management sets the common way risks are assessed and reported across the company; the process-safety and other EHS risks themselves are managed here.
evidence: Scope note only: the old area name is replaced by Legal & External Affairs (DSBP-DEC-0029), and the reciprocal sentence for Enterprise Risk Management is added; the definition is unchanged

label: Terminal Loading
definition: Control the lifting of product at a terminal: authorize the customers, carriers and drivers who may lift, take in customers' lifting forecasts and nominations, enforce at the loading rack how much each customer may lift, and capture the terminal sales deals behind the liftings, so that only authorized liftings within agreed limits take place.
scope_note: It is part of Terminal Services. Physical loading at the rack belongs to Terminal Operations Management. Plan-level allocation belongs to Allocate Finished Products, order-level allocation and release to Allocate & Release Order, and credit decisions and holds to Manage Credit & Risk; Terminal Loading enforces their results at the terminal (DSBP-DEC-0049).
evidence: glp-10k, Item 1, Wholesale: customers use their own vehicles or contract carriers to take delivery at bulk terminals and inland storage; dino-10k, Items 1 and 2, Refinery Operations: on-site truck and rail racks give access to local product markets; mplx-10k, Item 1, Our Crude Oil and Products Logistics Contracts: terminal services agreements; the four controls (authorization, nominations, rack allocation limits, sales deals) are the work of its four children, as DSBP-DEC-0049 records (evidence class I)

scope_note: Includes IT strategy, applications, data, infrastructure and the management of cybersecurity risk. Defining and improving business processes is Business Process Excellence; this area supplies the technology they use. Enterprise Risk Management sets the common way risks are assessed and reported; cybersecurity risk itself is managed here.

label: Lubricants & Specialties
definition: Make, package, sell and deliver finished lubricants, base oils and specialty products.
scope_note: Includes base oil and finished lubricant manufacture, blending and packaging, specialty products such as waxes, white oils and solvents, and their marketing and delivery. Fuels made in the same refinery belong to Refining. A company without this business leaves this area empty.
